newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Growers see more rain in key Brazil soybean areas.
newsitem.headline: Growers see more rain in key Brazil soybean areas.

text.p: Conditions were stable in Brazil's key soybean growing regions, with growers expecting some rain over the weekend and a new cold front in the south at the start of next week.

"A cold front arrived yesterday and we had 60 mm of rain," said Joao Henrich, agronomist at the Cotriba cooperative in Ibiruba, Rio Grande do Sul state. "Today it is sunny but we expect more rain over the weekend."
Regular showers this week had normalised soil moisture in most areas, cooperatives said.
"We have had regular rain since Sunday, a total of 100 mm," said Marcos Ricardo Streck, agronomist at the Cotrican cooperative in Candelaria. "The situation has normalised."
But he added that the so-called precocious cycle soybean crop had suffered a loss of 10 percent due to previous dryness.
Temperatures in Rio Grande do Sul were around 23 degrees Celsius and humidity was around 90 percent, growers reported.
In Parana, some farmers had already started to harvest the precocious cycle crop to take advantage of a lull in rains.

"It's quiet," said Otmar Hubner at the Parana agricultural secretariat. "It stopped raining two or three days ago but we're expecting more rain at the weekend and farmers have started the harvest in some regions to try to avoid it."
Two weeks of heavy rains had not caused any crop loss. "The potential for productivity is very good," Hubner said.
